standard_prerequisites.name: Left and right inverse types
standard_prerequisites.statement: The type of left inverses of f is the type of maps g with g composed with f equal to the identity, and the type of right inverses is the same with the composite in the other order.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two types shown contractible.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibre of a precomposition map
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fibre of the map sending h to h composed with f over the identity is exactly the type of left inverses of f, up to the equivalence supplied by function extensionality.
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the inverse type with a fibre.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibres of equivalences are contractible
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fibre of a map that is an equivalence over any point is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It finishes each of the two cases.

core_obligations: Use function extensionality to identify the type of left inverses of f with the fibre of the precomposition map over the identity (source lines 323-325).

Show that precomposition with f is an equivalence, using the cited results on composition of equivalences, the equivalence between being an equivalence and being an isomorphism, and the contractibility of the half adjoint equivalence structure (source lines 325-326).
Conclude contractibility of that fibre and repeat the same argument with postcomposition for the type of right inverses (source lines 326-328).

proof_roadmap.step: Turn the left inverse type into a fibre of a precomposition map.
Show that precomposition map is an equivalence.
Conclude contractibility and repeat for right inverses.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 319-321 (book Lemma 4.2.9): if a map f : A to B has a quasi-inverse, then both the type of left inverses of f and the type of right inverses of f are contractible. The statement is a contractibility claim about two auxiliary types, and the proof (source lines 322-328) has to recognise each of them as the fibre of a pre- or postcomposition map over the identity, which needs function extensionality, then to show that those composition maps are equivalences, which is where the cited results on composition of equivalences, on equivalences versus isomorphisms and on half adjoint equivalences are used, and finally to invoke the contractibility of fibres of equivalences. The identification of the two inverse types with those fibres is the whole reduction and it is absent from the statement.
